tools.name: list_formats
tools.description: Which formats conved.com converts. Prefer "from" (a format id or file extension, e.g. "docx", "heic"): the target formats for that source. Without arguments: the categories and their number of formats; with "category": the formats of that category (id → name). There are hundreds of formats, so avoid

tools.name: convert
tools.description: Convert one file to another format (one file in, one file out). Input – exactly one of: "url" (a public http(s) link), "text" + "filename" (source as text, e.g. Markdown, HTML, CSV, SVG; max 1 MB), "data_base64" + "filename" (a small binary file). For a file on the user's computer use create_upload

tools.name: create_upload
tools.description: Get a file that is not at a public URL into a conversion to "to". Returns a one-time link (1 hour, one file, counts toward the limits like convert) in two forms: (1) upload_page – a web page where the USER picks the file in the browser; use it when the file is on the user's computer and you cannot r

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Status of a conversion: "waiting", "done" (with download_url and expires_at; for "to": "pdfa" also "validation" – the PDF/A-2b conformance check by an independent validator: compliant, failed_rules, issues) or "error" (with an error code, e.g. timeout, killed, tool_error, empty_output, unsupported,

tools.name: list_jobs
tools.description: Recent conversions, newest first (id, file name, formats, status, time): those made through this connection (with a personal API token: all API conversions of the account). Use get_job for the download link.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: The account e-mail and limits. plan: "free" (limit per hour) or "custom" (limit per 24 hours). hourLimit / usedHour count conversions in the last 60 minutes, dailyLimit / usedToday in the last 24 hours (rolling windows, not calendar days); maxFileMb is the maximum file size. 0 in any limit means no

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "get_job" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: convert, create_upload, get_job · Private data: list_formats, convert, create_upload, get_job, list_jobs, get_account · Public sink: convert, create_upload, get_job · Destructive: list_formats, convert, create_upload.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: convert, create_upload, get_job · Private data: list_formats, convert, create_upload, get_job, list_jobs, get_account · Public sink: convert, create_upload, get_job · Destructive: list_formats, convert, create_upload

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
